articles.title: Hunting JavaScript Memory Leaks with Firefox DevTools: Heap Snapshots, Timers, and Event Listeners
articles.excerpt: Memory leaks in browser JavaScript are subtle, often hard to reproduce, and can cause tabs to gradually consume gigabytes of RAM. Firefox's DevTools have excellent memory analysis tools. This guide sh…
articles.body: Memory leaks in browser JavaScript are subtle, often hard to reproduce, and can cause tabs to gradually consume gigabytes of RAM. Firefox's DevTools have excellent memory analysis tools. This guide shows how to find and fix common memory leak patterns using Firefox's Memory and Performance panels. What Counts as a Memory Leak in JS A JavaScript memory leak is memory that's allocated but can't be garbage collected because references still exist, even though the code no longer needs that data. The GC can only free memory that's unreachable — leaked objects remain reachable via some reference chain.

articles.body: The green checkmark is not the story. The story is what broke while everything stayed green. Dominique Siacci, CTO of GoodBarber, published a post-mortem on dev.to on October 15, 2026, covering a six-day autonomous refactor of his company's app designer ( https://dev.to/dsiacci/964-hours-of-agent-work-in-six-days-heres-where-my-own-hours-went-13oc ). The headline numbers are the kind that get reposted: 28 coding agents, up to 20 running at once, 964 hours of session time, more than 6,000 commits, 717 deployments to the dev environment, and a final campaign of 12,074 end-to-end cases with zero gaps. The 200 templates he scoped turned out to be 569 units of work; 445 of them shipped. Then there is a section titled "What broke." Five items. Not one of them produced a red build.

articles.title: Responsive Power Apps in 2026: Containers, Breakpoints and Wrap
articles.excerpt: Many canvas apps pin every control to absolute X/Y coordinates at one design size, and look wrong at any other: a label overlapping a button on a laptop, dead space on a tablet, horizontal scrolling o…
articles.body: Many canvas apps pin every control to absolute X / Y coordinates at one design size, and look wrong at any other: a label overlapping a button on a laptop, dead space on a tablet, horizontal scrolling on a phone. Power Apps has had proper responsive layout tools — horizontal and vertical layout containers — for several years. Here's how to build screens that adapt, and the limits worth knowing before you commit to a layout. Why fixed positioning breaks A control with X: 850, Y: 120, Width: 300 is correct for exactly one screen size. With Scale to fit on, Power Apps' answer to other sizes is to render your app at its design resolution and scale the whole thing like an image: text gets smaller, touch targets shrink, and a phone shows a miniature desktop app.

articles.title: Give Your Coding Agent a Governed CLI Workflow with apexe
articles.excerpt: An agent task starts simply: list a directory, read a file, inspect a tool. As the task grows, those small calls become a workflow with real permissions and side effects. That is a useful place to int…
articles.body: An agent task starts simply: list a directory, read a file, inspect a tool. As the task grows, those small calls become a workflow with real permissions and side effects. That is a useful place to introduce apexe : a governed execution layer for CLI tools and HTTP APIs. It gives existing commands typed contracts and applies configured policy before execution, with records of executions and refusals. Here is how to start with a local CLI workflow, then connect it to the agent or protocol client you use. 1. Prepare apexe and a trusted CLI Use a prebuilt binary , or build from source with stable Rust and Cargo: git clone https://github.com/aiperceivable/apexe.git cd apexe cargo install --path . apexe --version The workflow below targets Unix CLI tools.

articles.body: Design a hotel booking system: the system design interview walkthrough The request to design a hotel booking system sounds like one line — list places, let guests book them — and that one line hides the whole interview. articles.title: It's time to reassess the size of our solar system, scientists say
articles.excerpt: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system based on the Milky Way's gravity, including its dark matter.
articles.body: Two leading space scientists say there is a need to redefine the edge of the solar system by presenting a theory which states that measurements of the Milky Way's gravitational field, including its dark matter, redraws the sun's frontier. That theory was put forward by Jim Green, former NASA chief scientist and past director of the space agency's Planetary Science Division, along with Ed Belbruno, a professor of mathematics at Yeshiva University and a senior research associate at Princeton University. The solar system's gravitational frontier extends to nearly 3.8 light-years from the sun , they contend, roughly 241,000 astronomical units (AU), a distance that brings the "edge" of the solar system to within the same scale as the separation between neighboring stars.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.
